SID OBSERVATORY / THIRD PRESSING

Listen closer.

A demoscene listening room with a view into the Commodore 64’s Sound Interface Device.

This prototype uses Hermit’s jsSID 0.9.1, adapted to an AudioWorklet. Voice traces and envelope levels come from the emulator; register values are sampled for display. Phosphor mode maps those samples to glowing radial orbits with a short history of fading traces. Oscilloscope mode shows triggered, flat waveforms. Reduced-motion mode keeps the radial geometry but removes orbit rotation and history trails.

Supported here: PAL PSID music with a callable play routine, subtunes, voice mute/solo and 6581/8580 emulation chosen per chip. 2SID and 3SID tunes (PSID v3/v4) play with one filter and one model selector per chip; the selector starts on the model the file declares. RSID, NTSC and ROM-dependent tunes are not supported. This lightweight engine is not a cycle-exact reference player.

ADSR readouts are raw 4-bit register values. The envelope meter is the emulator’s internal envelope level; the SID only exposes ENV3 directly on real hardware. Cutoff is shown as an 11-bit register value, not a measured frequency.

No music is bundled with the site. Imported files are not uploaded or stored after you close the page.

Archive tunes are fetched from the High Voltage SID Collection (HVSC) directly into your browser when you choose them, and are never stored by this site. The browsable index and song lengths are built from HVSC’s own Songlengths database for one pinned release. All tunes remain the copyright of their composers and publishers; HVSC distributes them for private enjoyment only.
